acceptance: Qualification covers C={1,2,4,8,16} for feasible profiles and C=32 for appropriate server-class systems.
Reports include throughput, latency percentiles, fairness, errors, resource pressure, and session-pool evidence.
A platform cannot publish a lower actual concurrency under a higher C label.
Recommended public concurrency points are supported by saturation and stability evidence.
The complete measured curve remains publishable next to any selected headline point.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. The ADR's numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, and M4 reference are pilot hypotheses until the methodology-freeze item closes.
description: Run the declared concurrency ladder against qualified dataset profiles. Identify saturation, instability, memory pressure, unfairness, and platform/session limitations; retain full curves and recommend display points instead of assuming S/C4, M/C8, and L/C16.
